title: Janpath Market Delhi - Street Shopping, Timings & Travel Guide
content:
Janpath Market - Delhi,

Janpath Market is one of the most famous street shopping destinations in Delhi, located near Connaught Place. Popular among college students, tourists, and bargain lovers, the market is filled with colorful stalls offering trendy clothes, jewelry, handicrafts, home décor, and souvenirs. Its affordable prices and lively atmosphere make it a must-visit for anyone exploring Delhi.

History & Overview:

The word “Janpath” means People’s Path, and the market has been living up to its name for decades. Starting as a small line of shops, it has grown into a bustling marketplace for budget shopping. Today, it’s a blend of ethnic handicrafts and modern fashion, drawing both locals and international tourists.

What Makes It Special:

Janpath is often called a shopper’s paradise. From bohemian clothes and tribal jewelry to handmade artifacts and Kashmiri woolens, it offers something for everyone. The best part is the pocket-friendly pricing – but remember, bargaining is a must here.

Things to Shop For:

  • Trendy clothes and western wear,
  • Traditional Indian handicrafts,
  • Jewelry and accessories,
  • Kashmiri shawls, stoles, and carpets,
  • Handbags and leather items,
  • Souvenirs and home decor pieces,

Food & Eateries:

After shopping, visitors can enjoy street food and nearby cafés. You’ll find vendors selling chaat, momos, and golgappas, along with popular cafés in Connaught Place like Saravana Bhavan, Wenger’s, and Cafe Coffee Day.

Entry Fee & Timings:

  • Entry Fee: Free,
  • Timings: 11:00 AM – 8:00 PM (Open all days),

How to Reach:

  • Nearest Metro Station: Janpath Metro Station (Violet Line) or Rajiv Chowk Metro Station (Yellow Line)
  • By Road: Well-connected via buses, autos, and cabs.
  • Parking: Limited parking available near Connaught Place and Janpath Road.

Places to Visit Nearby:

  • Connaught Place,
  • Jantar Mantar,
  • Agrasen ki Baoli,
  • Bangla Sahib Gurudwara,

Travel Tips:

  • Always bargain – prices can be marked up for tourists.
  • Carry some cash as not all vendors accept cards/UPI.
  • Be cautious with your belongings in crowded areas.
  • Visit nearby attractions to make the most of your trip.
excerpt: Janpath Market is a lively and colorful street market in Delhi, best known for budget shopping, handicrafts, and trendy clothes. With its central location near Connaught Place and nearby attractions like Jantar Mantar and Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, it’s a must-visit for both locals and tourists.
